headline: Every bag of coffee checked, not a sample.
label: #F7F3EC
heroLede: Seven Seeds roasts at its Fairfield roastery on Montefiore Street and supplies cafés through its wholesale portal. When several coffees go into bags that look the same, a quick check by eye can miss a mix-up. This is what a camera check could look like on a coffee bagging line. Scroll through, then adjust the estimate at the end to your own numbers.
lidLede: The camera checks every bag is sealed straight across with the one-way valve in place. A bag that is not sealed properly lets the coffee go stale long before the café opens it.
labelLede: Bags of different coffees look the same until you read the label. The camera checks every bag carries the right label for the blend, so a decaf drinker never gets a full-strength bag.
codeLede: Cafés and home brewers look for the roast date before anything else. The system reads the printed roast date and batch code on every bag and compares them with the blend and date set at changeover.
objectLede: Loose beans, valve backing papers and tape can all end up on the belt. The camera over the conveyor spots anything that should not be there before it reaches a carton.

vocab.ok: Seal, label and roast date OK
vocab.alert: Four creased seals in fifteen minutes. Check the heat sealer.
